acv.quote: About a hundred and forty K a year.

data.reason: The deal turned when Wen used one month of Tallowfield's own statements to put a yearly dollar cost on the manual deposit matching, and the CFO accepted it as 'my number, not yours.' Dana's lesson is to find the CFO sooner, but the evidence shows the deciding step was pricing the problem in the customer's own numbers. Dana had the deal at 20 percent just before that meeting.

trigger.finding: The inbound looked like an online ordering portal project, but the real trigger was a new CFO whose first month-end close took nine days, partly because two people matched deposits by hand. Here our messaging would have landed better aimed at a new finance leader's first painful close than at the portal launch.
trigger.quote: She'd been there about four months, and her first month-end close took nine days.

decider.finding: Ines, the CFO, made the call and signed; Paul, the IT director and our day-to-day contact, said so himself. Our first proposal only reached her through Paul, and she dismissed it after the first page, so our champion was not the decider and we reached her late.

competitor.finding: Fiserv was the incumbent through the customer's bank, and the AE didn't know what Fiserv showed, if anything. Ines said the bank answered her by offering to look at rates, and afterwards her one new question to us was whether she'd get a named contact, because her bank rep had changed. That suggests the incumbent was weak on the problem and on attention, not on price.
competitor.quote: I didn't ask about my rates.

message.finding: The standard deck got silence: 'Financial infrastructure, global growth, all the currencies' meant nothing to a three-state distributor. The developer story went nowhere with a four-person IT team running an off-the-shelf portal. The payout reconciliation demo, tying each payout to transactions and the ERP, made Ines stop the demo and ask to see it with their data. For this buyer, reconciliation was the lead message, not checkout or APIs.

proof.finding: Ines asked twice to speak with another distributor, and we only had retail and software stories. She dismissed the retail case study we sent. The branch counter readers feeding the same report were shown on a slide but never demoed. This points to a gap in wholesale and distributor proof.
proof.quote: this is a company that sells sweaters.

words.finding: Ines talked about knowing where her money is, 'the deposits' and 'a week of archaeology'. She never said 'payments', and nobody said 'infrastructure'. In this deal, the buyer's words were about visibility of deposits and month-end pain, not our platform vocabulary.
words.quote: I just want to know where my money is.
